body.explanation: With the default FIFO queue, UDP fills the sender queue and tail-drops TCP; TCP inflight stays at one segment and RTO stalls, so tcp_goodput_bps is 0. Replacing the sender-side FIFO with a per-flow scheduler gives TCP a round-robin service share, about half the 1 Gbps link after packet overhead. Loss-based TCP variants fill that share and deliver about 482 Mbps; Bbr and Vegas underfill it and deliver less. Queue length 100 is enough to keep the scheduler share filled; larger queues do not increase delivered goodput.
